title: Data for studying sonority / Sound level protrusions as physical correlates of sonority
why_promising: Primary non-singing English and Spanish production recorded in 2005 and linked directly to Parker's Journal of Phonetics study. The public Mendeley Data record states that the WAV recordings were manually segmented and analyzed in Praat, documents 44.1-kHz recording and equipment details, and releases the deposit under CC BY 4.0. This is promising for source-level speech, manually delimited sonority-related intervals, amplitude/sound-level measures, and cross-language production.
open_question: The public landing page currently describes the deposit as raw WAV files and does not enumerate annotation/measurement filenames in the rendered file section. Keep in review until the downloadable bundle/API is enumerated to establish whether the manual segment boundaries and derived measurements themselves are publicly deposited. If only WAV is present, retain the source reference but do not admit unobservable manual measurements into core.
